extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: The Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD) is a synthetic texture image dataset containing 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, generated using text-to-image models (Stable Diffusion) guided by descriptive prompts. It was created to support texture-based research tasks including texture bias analysis, model interpretability, and adversarial robustness studies, offering greater diversity than existing real-image texture datasets.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak (University of Wisconsin-Madison); Patrick McDaniel (University of Wisconsin-Madison)
extraction.citeAs: Blaine Hoak and Patrick McDaniel. On Synthetic Texture Datasets: Challenges, Creation, and Curation. arXiv:2409.10297v3 [cs.CV], 9 May 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by generating texture images using the Stable Diffusion text-to-image model, guided by 96,768 unique text prompts constructed from combinations of texture class descriptors and artistic/spatial/color attributes. Five images were generated per prompt, producing 483,840 images before refinement, which were then filtered down to 246,285 images through a three-stage refinement process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Up to 60% of initially generated images were flagged as NSFW by Stable Diffusion's content safety filter and replaced with black screens; these flagged images were excluded from the final dataset and not released publicly, resulting in gaps in coverage for certain texture classes and prompt descriptors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images generated by the Stable Diffusion model (accessed via HuggingFace) using 96,768 unique text prompts derived from 56 texture classes combined with artistic, spatial, color enhancer, and color descriptors. Texture classes were sourced from the Describable Textures Dataset (DTD) and supplementary texture word lists.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 9 participants were recruited to evaluate images from the dataset. Each participant was shown 100 images in random order and asked two questions per image: (1) How would you rate the overall quality of the image? and (2) How well does the image represent the provided descriptor? Ratings were on a scale of 1 to 5. Images were selected randomly with no duplicates between or within sets, covering 900 unique images. Images were selected before the refinement stage so that pre- and post-refinement scores could be compared.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Mean quality and representativeness scores were computed across images at each stage of the refinement process. Results were compared across refinement steps to assess improvement. CLIP scores were also validated against human representative scores to confirm alignment.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stable Diffusion (for image generation); CLIP (for CLIP score filtering and representativeness measurement); Inception model (for Inception Score evaluation); Fourier transform analysis (for frequency filtering)
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Textures that more often appear in common objects (e.g., hairy, flaky) tend to have better Inception and FID scores, while more structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted) tend to have worse scores, indicating room for improvement in generating structured textures; certain descriptor combinations (e.g., 'muted', 'earthy') yield lower quality images
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Stable Diffusion models are not explicitly designed to create textures, so object-like images may arise during generation; up to 60% of initial generated images were flagged as NSFW by the safety filter despite benign prompts, requiring regeneration; more structured textures show lower quality scores indicating room for improvement; Inception and FID metrics were originally designed for object-based datasets and may not fully capture texture dataset quality
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset can be used to uncover texture bias in machine learning models, contributing to model trustworthiness and interpretability; the work highlights the need for refined NSFW filters that can better handle abstract or texture-based content
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains synthetically generated texture images and does not contain personal or sensitive information; images flagged as NSFW by the safety filter were excluded from the final dataset and not released publicly
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of texture-based machine learning research; measuring texture bias in models; constructing texture-object associations; studying adversarial examples based on texture patterns; supporting interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness research in machine learning
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images flagged as NSFW by the Stable Diffusion safety filter were excluded from the dataset and regenerated to ensure a consistent number of images per prompt (5 non-flagged images per prompt), resulting in 483,840 images before refinement. The dataset was then filtered down through a three-stage refinement process: (1) frequency filtering retaining the top 80% of images with the highest frequency cutoff values per texture class to remove object-like images; (2) patch variance filtering removing the bottom 20% of images with the lowest mean patch variance per texture class to eliminate homogeneous images; and (3) CLIP score filtering removing the bottom 20% of images with the lowest CLIP scores per texture class to ensure prompt alignment. The final dataset contains 246,285 images balanced across all 56 texture classes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied to the generated images: (1) Frequency filtering: images were filtered based on Fourier transform power spectrum analysis, retaining only the top 80% of images with the highest frequency cutoff values (fc) within each texture class to remove object-like images; (2) Patch variance filtering: images were divided into non-overlapping 50x50 pixel patches, mean intensity per patch was computed, and the bottom 20% of images with the lowest mean patch variance within each texture class were removed to eliminate homogeneous or near-uniform images; (3) CLIP score filtering: the bottom 20% of images with the lowest CLIP scores within each texture class were removed to ensure alignment with descriptive prompts. Additionally, images flagged as NSFW by the Stable Diffusion safety filter were excluded from the final dataset.
